props.gloss_en: it is written: 'and God made the two great lights' (Gen 1:16)
and it is written: 'the great light ... and the lesser light'
R' Shimon ben Pazi's resolution: the two lights were made great, and the moon was then told to diminish herself -- so both verses hold, at two moments
the moon: Master of the world, can two kings make use of one crown?
the Holy One: go and diminish yourself
the moon: because I said a proper thing before You, must I diminish myself?
the Holy One: go and rule by day and by night
the moon: what greatness is that? what use is a lamp at noon?
the Holy One: go -- Israel will count days and years by you
the moon: by the sun too it is impossible that they not count the seasons
'and they shall be for signs and for seasons and for days and years' (Gen 1:14)
the Holy One: go -- the righteous will be called by your name: Yaakov ha-katan, Shmuel ha-katan, David ha-katan
seeing she was not appeased, the Holy One said: bring atonement for Me, for I diminished the moon
Resh Lakish: why is the New-Moon goat singled out with 'to the Lord' (Num 28:15)? The Holy One said: this goat shall be an atonement for My diminishing the moon
it is written 'and the earth brought forth grass' (Gen 1:12) -- on the third day
and it is written 'no shrub of the field was yet in the earth' (Gen 2:5) -- on Sabbath eve
Rav Asi: this teaches that the grasses came out and stood at the opening of the ground until Adam came and prayed for them, and rain fell and they sprouted
Rav Asi: to teach you that the Holy One desires the prayer of the righteous
Rav Nachman bar Pappa had a garden; he sowed seeds and nothing sprouted; he prayed, rain came and it sprouted
